title: Bilinear maps extend through module sheafification
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $\mathcal O$ be a presheaf of commutative rings with sheafification $\mathcal O\to\mathcal O^\#$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be presheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] with module sheafifications $\mathcal F\to\mathcal F^\#$, $\mathcal G\to\mathcal G^\#$, sheaves of $\mathcal O^\#$-modules [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface], and let $\mathcal H$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal O^\#$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], regarded as a presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules by restriction of scalars. Every morphism of presheaves of sets $\beta:\mathcal F\times\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ that is $\mathcal O$-bilinear on sections extends uniquely to a morphism of sheaves of sets $\beta^\#:\mathcal F^\#\times\mathcal G^\#\to\mathcal H$ that is $\mathcal O^\#$-bilinear and satisfies $\beta^\#\circ(\mathcal F\times\mathcal G\to\mathcal F^\#\times\mathcal G^\#)=\beta$.

source.place: Lemma 18.26.2 (Tag 0GMW), hint using universal property of sheafification

proof.text: By [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets], the underlying sheaves of sets of the abelian sheafifications $\mathcal F^\#$, $\mathcal G^\#$ (with the units) are the sheafifications of the underlying presheaves of sets of $\mathcal F$, $\mathcal G$, and likewise for $\mathcal O\to\mathcal O^\#$ as presheaf of rings; so all sheafifications below may be taken in sheaves of sets. The presheaf map $\beta:\mathcal F\times\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ has sheaf target. By the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], it factors uniquely through a morphism $\widetilde\beta:(\mathcal F\times\mathcal G)^\#\to\mathcal H$ whose composite with the sheafification unit is $\beta$.

source.place: Lemma 18.26.1 (Tag 0GMW), hint using universal property of sheafification

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact], whose site-size hypothesis is part of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], the product of the two sheafifications is canonically isomorphic to $(\mathcal F\times\mathcal G)^\#$, compatibly with both units. Define $\beta^\#$ as $\widetilde\beta$ after this canonical isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 18.26.1 (Tag 0GMW), hint using the sheafification universal property

proof.text: To check $\mathcal O^\#$-bilinearity, compare the two sheaf maps expressing additivity and scalar compatibility after precomposition with the sheafification units. By the product comparison [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact], these precompositions (along the set-sheafification units of $\mathcal O\times\mathcal F\times\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal F\times\mathcal F\times\mathcal G$, which by [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets] are the products of the module and ring sheafification units) come from the corresponding maps on $\mathcal O\times\mathcal F\times\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal F\times\mathcal G$, where they agree because $\beta$ is $\mathcal O$-bilinear. The compatible $\mathcal O^\#$-actions are those of [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface], so the equalities descend uniquely through sheafification.

source.place: Lemma 18.26.1 (Tag 0GMW), hint using the sheafification universal property

proof.text: For uniqueness, any other extension composed with the product isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact] gives a map $(\mathcal F\times\mathcal G)^\#\to\mathcal H$ whose composite with the sheafification unit is $\beta$. The uniqueness clause of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] forces it to equal $\widetilde\beta$, hence forces the other extension to equal $\beta^\#$; the compatibility with the units gives the stated restriction identity.

source.place: Lemma 18.26.1 (Tag 0GMW), hint using the sheafification universal property
